stories.headline: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers for Senate, two days before the vote
stories.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, appeared with GOP nominee Mike Rogers at a Detroit church on Sunday and then endorsed him in a video. She said El-Sayed had told her she was no longer welcome at his events. She has criticized him over his past campaigning with streamer Hasan Piker and over an ad by Cenk Uygur blaming Israel for high grocery prices; El-Sayed's campaign says it had nothing to do with the ad and criticized it. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called the move a "despicable betrayal"; El-Sayed told reporters it doesn't matter to voters. Trump praised her at his Iowa rally.
stories.why: Michigan's open seat is one of the races that decides whether Democrats can win the Senate, and the split exposes a wider Democratic rift over Israel.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Judge throws out DOJ bid to set aside 'second Dan Sullivan' ballots in Alaska; DOJ appeals
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason on Sunday dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to separate ballots cast for little-known candidate Daniel J. Sullivan and to hold off certifying the Senate race if Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan loses. She wrote that the request would violate Alaskans' right to a secret ballot. The department said it will appeal. Republicans allege Democrat Mary Peltola's camp recruited the second Sullivan to confuse voters; Peltola denies it. Separately, California Gov. Gavin Newsom on Oct 31 wrote to the state's four chief federal judges warning they may be asked for warrants to seize ballots before results are certified.
stories.why: Courts are now refereeing how votes are counted and certified in races that could decide control of Congress.
stories.label: Fact + allegation
stories.note: Ongoing: an earlier ruling against DOJ pressure on election officials was in Edition 1 (Nov 1).

stories.headline: Trump closes the campaign in Iowa and Kansas as GOP defends its majorities

stories.headline: NYC voters: five city charter questions are on the back of Tuesday's ballot
stories.summary: Besides the races for Congress and state offices, New York City ballots carry five yes-or-no charter amendments from the Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE), the 2026 charter review commission: (1) faster permits for sidewalk cafes, ramps and planters; (2) less contractor paperwork; (3) quicker street-safety projects, sales of unused city property and office leasing, with City Planning Commission approval instead of a Council vote on property sales; (4) a central construction-permit hub at the Buildings Department; and (5) a target for the city's rainy-day reserves. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Nov 3.
stories.why: Question 3 in particular would shift some land-sale decisions away from the City Council, so it's worth reading before you vote.

stories.headline: Carney and Trump talk trade; teams to work on a deal 'in the coming weeks'

Trump said there is "the concept of a deal" that would be good for U.S. farmers and "fine for Canada." stories.headline: Alberta's elections chief says: keep the old riding map or delay the 2027 vote
stories.summary: In a letter dated Oct 30, Chief Electoral Officer Gordon McClure told MLAs that Elections Alberta needs 12 to 18 months to run an election on new boundaries and cannot prepare for two maps at once, so the Oct 18, 2027 election should use current boundaries or be postponed. A contested boundary report is due in the legislature Monday. NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi says the proposed map gerrymanders Calgary and Lethbridge and vows a court challenge; Premier Danielle Smith denies manipulating the vote. The justice minister's office says it is reviewing the letter.
stories.why: It raises the prospect of Alberta's next election being delayed amid a fight over fair representation.
stories.label: Fact + allegation

stories.headline: Ottawa quietly shelves the 'Jane Goodall Act' on elephant and great ape captivity
stories.summary: The bill, which would have banned new captivity, breeding and import or export of elephants and great apes except for conservation, welfare or research, passed the Senate in 2024 but died when Parliament was prorogued in January 2025. Despite a 2025 Liberal campaign pledge, the environment minister's office told CBC no decision has been made to reintroduce it. Advocates suspect the government's focus on the tariff war. About 23 elephants live in Canada.
stories.why: Ottawa says zoos and animal welfare are mainly provincial matters, so for now there's no national rule on keeping these animals.
stories.label: Fact + opinion

stories.headline: Communist Party publishes plenum resolution tightening oversight of officials and their families
stories.summary: Xinhua released the full resolution on "full and rigorous Party self-governance" adopted at the fifth plenum. It calls for tighter career-long oversight of officials, starting with senior ranks, checks on those whose family assets or spending far exceed their income, closer watch on business activities of officials' spouses and children, and a drive against nepotism. In an accompanying explanation, Xi Jinping said misconduct and "hidden dangers" persist; the SCMP notes he argued strict discipline does not stifle growth.
stories.why: It sets the tone for Party discipline ahead of next year's Party congress, where a leadership reshuffle is expected.
stories.label: Fact (state media)

Russian media reported the site was closed and evacuated. stories.headline: Rioting and looting in Frankfurt after Germany's 'Gen Z' protests; 100+ police hurt
stories.summary: Tens of thousands joined largely peaceful 'Gen Z regelt' rallies in German cities on Saturday over school funding, living costs and military conscription. In Frankfurt, rioters later damaged 17 shops and looted five, attacking police with stones, fireworks and petrol bombs. Police arrested 54 people aged 13 to 29; more than 100 officers were injured. Hesse's interior minister said most suspects were German nationals but many had immigrant backgrounds; the city's mayor said passports don't matter, only accountability. Organisers condemned the violence and plan to join Europe-wide protests on Nov 20.
stories.why: It follows riots in France last month, as a youth protest wave spreads across Europe.

stories.headline: Tai Po fire report faults inspectors; housing chief Winnie Ho resigns
stories.summary: Hong Kong released the independent committee's report on last November's Wang Fuk Court fire, which killed 168 people. It heavily faulted the Housing Bureau's inspection unit. Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned to take political responsibility, and leader John Lee and officials bowed in apology. Some survivors told HKFP the apology lacked sincerity.
stories.why: It is the city's deadliest fire in decades, and the findings drive sweeping building-safety reforms.
stories.label: Fact + opinion
stories.note: The released report is redacted; criminal cases over the fire are ongoing.

stories.headline: Hong Kong moves to make renovation bid-rigging a crime and scraps disgraced inspection unit
stories.summary: The government proposed making bid-rigging, price-fixing and similar collusion in building-repair tenders a criminal offence with up to 10 years in jail. It also said the faulted inspection unit will be replaced within about a month by a new section, with its roughly 300 staff moving over.
stories.why: Triad-linked bid-rigging in renovations was flagged by the fire inquiry as a serious problem.
stories.label: Fact (proposal)
stories.note: The criminal offence is a proposal; RTHK reports the target is to pass it by April.

stories.headline: Eight firms, including Uber and Didi, apply for Hong Kong's first ride-hailing licences
stories.summary: The Transport Department received eight applications before Friday's deadline under the city's new ride-hailing rules. Uber, Tada, Amap and Didi confirmed they applied, and the first approvals are expected in late November or early December.
stories.why: Ride-hailing has operated in a legal grey zone in Hong Kong for years.

stories.headline: Hong Kong just had its warmest October since records began in 1884
stories.summary: The Observatory said October's mean temperature was 27.6°C, with the average high and low also setting October records. It blamed a very strong El Niño and a weak northeast monsoon, with climate change also playing a role. A cooler monsoon is expected early this week.
stories.why: Record heat is becoming routine, even in what is normally a mild month.

stories.summary: The inaugural race ran from Shek Mun through Tai Po and the Lung Shan Tunnel to the new Fanling Bypass. Runners said the heat was tough and some complained about too few water stations. Organizers hope to hold future races in cooler months and may extend the route toward Shenzhen.

stories.headline: China's factories shrank again in October, the third contraction in four months
stories.summary: The official manufacturing index fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September; below 50 means contraction. Reuters reports weaker demand at home and cooling export orders, and economists urged more support for growth.
stories.why: Exports have carried China's economy this year, and that engine is showing strain.
stories.label: Fact + analysis

stories.headline: China's Zhang Haiqin wins 53kg gold at home weightlifting worlds by one kilogram
stories.summary: At the IWF World Championships in Ningbo, Zhang totalled 221kg (98kg snatch, 123kg clean and jerk) to edge American Miranda Ulrey's 220kg. A final 126kg lift that would have broken the world standard failed. North Korea's Kim So Hyon took bronze.
stories.why: It is a home-soil world title in a new Olympic weight class at the start of the Los Angeles 2028 cycle.

stories.headline: China steps up patrols east of Taiwan and around Scarborough Shoal
stories.summary: China's coast guard said it ran law-enforcement patrols in waters east of Taiwan on Saturday, part of a rise in activity there since June. A day earlier, the military and coast guard patrolled around Scarborough Shoal, calling it a response to Philippine 'provocations' without giving details.
stories.why: Taiwanese officials say they believe China is rehearsing a possible blockade.
stories.label: Fact + allegation
stories.note: Blockade practice is Taiwan officials' assessment; Beijing calls the patrols routine.

stories.headline: Iran holds talks via Qatar as region braces for possible US strikes after the midterms
stories.summary: Iranian envoys met Qatari mediators in Doha on Saturday on ways to end the Gulf war, Reuters reported, citing a source. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump hasn't decided on new strikes and prefers diplomacy. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered the armed forces to respond immediately and without geographic limits to any attack.
stories.why: A return to fighting could hit oil prices and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Canelo Alvarez regains WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh
stories.summary: Mexico's Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez, 36, beat France's previously unbeaten Christian Mbilli by unanimous decision (115-112, 116-111, 117-110) in his first fight since losing to Terence Crawford in September 2025. stories.headline: Spain's deadliest high-speed rail crash kills 69; probe focuses on control center
stories.summary: A Renfe high-speed train slammed into a stopped Iryo train near Urda, south of Madrid, on Wednesday, killing at least 69 people. Investigators are looking at how the control center responded after a safety signaling system failed on the Madrid-Seville line.

stories.headline: Oleshky civilians reach Ukraine under a rare truce as Russian strikes cut power
stories.summary: Exhausted residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky crossed into Ukraine under a six-day local ceasefire mediated by US first lady Melania Trump with the Pope's involvement, after a long trip via Crimea, Russia and Belarus. Meanwhile, Russian strikes left tens of thousands without power, including in Kyiv.
stories.why: It is the first humanitarian truce of its kind in more than four years of war.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Mayon volcano erupts in the Philippines; 2,000+ evacuated
stories.summary: A moderately explosive eruption on Oct 30 sent ash 3 km high and put Mayon on Alert Level 3. More than 2,000 people were evacuated, and about 420 families spent All Saints' Day in evacuation centers.
stories.why: Mayon is the Philippines' most active volcano, and a bigger eruption would force more evacuations.
